stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Use the chapter’s definition of algebraic-space morphisms on the chosen big fppf site; a representable morphism has a property P only through all its scheme-base-change tests.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a representable morphism of
algebraic spaces over $S$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is universally submersive
(in the sense of Section \ref{section-representable}), and
\item for every morphism of algebraic spaces $Z \to Y$ the morphism of
topological spaces $|Z \times_Y X| \to |Z|$ is submersive.
\end{enumerate}

reason: After an étale scheme presentation of the target, universally submersive representable f is tested in a square with open surjective horizontal charts and surjective topological-fibre-product comparison. These transfer the quotient-topology condition to any algebraic-space base change, and the converse is by definition.
